decisions.summary: The found row hold_ring_rules#judged at the gate's lines is fixed by moving the re-hold to 0005's placer lines (25 deg, a quarter of the design cell), not by the row's alternative of recording the looser line as a DEVIATION and relabeling the claim.
decisions.why: FR-004: a fix moves the implementation to the research. The GM's request: 'I'm not sure there's any reason for our implementation to not match for anything.'

decisions.summary: The re-hold's choice of rings to re-hold (bad), the pieces it keeps and the weld hosts it accepts are all judged by held_faults (ring_violations plus the placer's lines) instead of ring_violations alone.
decisions.why: This is the found row's fix as written. It is bounded by the only= set the grave cut passes (settlement/fields/features.py:153), and it is what 0005's drawing page requires of every basin drawn ('No basin narrows to a point sharper than 25 degrees, none is a scrap under a quarter of the basin its field was cut to').

decisions.summary: held_faults also refuses an arrowhead (is_chevron at 40 deg / 0.90), a third line the found row's fix text did not name.
decisions.why: The same sentence of 0005 the claim points at names all three: '...and none is shaped like an arrowhead' (drawing page line 5; line 35 'The maps refuse a basin shaped like an arrowhead'). Moving the implementation closer to the research is the request's direction. 0005's comment that close_seams accepted a chevron as a last resort does not conflict: here a refused host leaves the scrap bare under the fan floor (the existing 'scrap left bare' claim), not a doubled bund.

decisions.summary: _split_steps' choice of cut, shared with the settle, still ranks candidate cuts by ring_violations' faults.
decisions.why: It picks a cut and keeps nothing itself. Every piece the re-hold keeps and every weld it makes passes held_faults, so no kept basin escapes the placer's lines. A cut chosen at the gate's lines can only send more pieces to the weld or to the bare-scrap path, which is a cost or quality question and not a narrowing of what was asked. Measured: the pool is byte-identical.

decisions.summary: The claim 'judged at the gate's lines' (which recorded the drift) is rewritten as 'judged at the placer's lines', and held_faults carries its own Research: claim to 0005.
decisions.why: The claim now states what the fixed code does, the code now matches 0005, and impl-drift found the re-hold's claims IN-STEP. This is FR-005's re-check, not the XVI rewrite path, because the code moved.

decisions.summary: m:wave78-rehold-placer-lines: the unit test, the five hamlets byte-identical, the 48-seed cohort as wave 77, impl-drift six IN-STEP with no claim owed.
decisions.why: Re-run by this reviewer: the test file passes 13/13. The pool manifests (pool/hamlets/*, 10:32-10:33) postdate the close.py edit (10:26) and git diff HEAD on pool/ is empty, so 'byte-identical' was measured on the fix. The cohort figure stands on the entry's record, not re-run. Tier order (SC-003): ranking.json holds no open E0 or E1 row that is not deferred, so an E2 row is next in order.
